page: Amazon Web Services i4g.large is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit Arm Neoverse-N1 architecture. The instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, eliminating resource contention from simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside a bundled 468 GB local NVMe solid-state drive. Networking capabilities feature a baseline throughput of 1 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest computational throughput, consistent with a low-core Arm configuration. Single-core processing in stress-ng registers in the middle tier at 1519.48, while multi-core metrics (3019.78 in stress-ng and 1749.0 in Geekbench) place the instance in the lower percentiles. Memory subsystem tests show uncached sequential read and write speeds of 37.47 GB/sec and 18.83 GB/sec, respectively. In-memory data workloads achieve 2.41 million Redis SET operations per second, while static web serving delivers 2.4 GB/sec.

From an efficiency perspective, the i4g.large trades high compute density for direct, low-latency local storage and a generous memory footprint per core. Because CPU scores across PassMark, Clang compilation, and machine learning inference are constrained by the dual-core boundary, this instance is not designed for compute-bound or parallel processing jobs. Instead, it offers an economical architecture for storage-bound environments requiring dedicated hardware cores, fast local NVMe transactions, and moderate memory capacity, such as intermediate database caching, logging agents, and read-heavy NoSQL datastores.
description: Amazon Web Services i4g.large is a storage-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 Arm64 processor. Operating under the Nitro System hypervisor, it features 2 dedicated physical vCPUs clocked at 2.5 GHz, 16.0 GB of system memory, and a direct-attached 468 GB NVMe SSD, backed by a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance delivers solid single-thread performance, though aggregate multi-threaded compute, memory bandwidth, and compilation scores reflect the limitations of its two-core profile. The pairing of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU with high-speed local NVMe storage creates an efficient operational envelope for I/O-sensitive workloads that do not demand extensive CPU parallelism. It is well-matched for localized transactional databases, search indexing nodes, distributed caching systems, and lightweight log aggregation services.
